lead: You’ve earned a brain break. Watch this very confident explanation of AI. Spoiler alert: every claim is false. The fun is seeing how wrong it gets.

claims.claim: AI reads your mind through your cell phone. That’s how its answers sound so personal.
claims.explain: AI uses your message and the context available to it to generate a response. It cannot read your mind.
claims.visual: A sketched phone sends colorful signal waves toward a cartoon thought bubble.
claims.extra: The phone in your pocket picks up your thoughts and sends them straight to the model. Forget typing. Just think louder.

claims.claim: AI tokens are arcade coins. Every time you ask a question, a tiny robot drops one into a machine.
claims.explain: In this course, tokens are pieces of text that AI processes as numbers. No arcade coins required.
claims.visual: A tiny sketched robot drops a coin into an arcade machine.
claims.extra: Long questions need a whole bucket of coins. This is why AI companies are always asking for more tokens.

claims.claim: Training an AI means making it run laps around a data center. The more laps it runs, the smarter it gets.
claims.explain: During training, AI adjusts its parameters using data. It learns through numerical updates, not exercise.
claims.visual: A computer wearing running shoes circles a row of server cabinets.
claims.extra: The best models train before breakfast. Nobody wants an AI that gets tired halfway through a homework question.

claims.claim: AI adds layers when it gets cold. Bigger models need bigger jackets.
claims.explain: Layers are processing stages that update the numbers inside the model. They are not clothing.
claims.visual: A computer is bundled in an oversized stack of colorful jackets.
claims.extra: Engineers keep data centers cool, so models need plenty of layers. A hundred-layer model has a very crowded closet.

claims.claim: Attention is how AI stays awake late at night, even after its bedtime.
claims.explain: Attention weighs information from related tokens. It has nothing to do with sleep.
claims.visual: A wide-eyed computer sits beside a crescent moon and an alarm clock.
claims.extra: Without attention, the model would fall asleep before finishing your answer. That is why it can help you at two in the morning.

claims.claim: ChatGPT and Gemini run on computer chips, but Claude runs on a special type of pasta called Claude-A-Roni.
claims.explain: Claude runs on computers too. The pasta-powered model is a joke.
claims.visual: ChatGPT and Gemini labels sit above computer chips; Claude sits above a bowl of rotini with a Claude-A-Roni label.
claims.extra: It is a proprietary rotini developed for advanced reasoning. For difficult questions, simply add more sauce.

close: Now you know how AI really works. Please do not put pasta in your computer.
